bill.title: Making National Parks Safer Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 469.

industries.rationale: The bill mandates installation of Next Generation 911 systems, which are internet-based telecommunications infrastructure that telecom providers typically supply and maintain.
NG911 systems are digital, internet protocol-based platforms requiring software, hardware, and IT services for implementation and operation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the National Park Service to assess the current state and costs of upgrading emergency call centers in national parks to Next Generation 911 systems. Based on that assessment, the Park Service must then develop a plan to install these modern, internet-based 911 systems at park emergency communications centers.

bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-12.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on social media platforms and user-generated content websites.
New criminal prohibitions and mandatory restitution provisions would generate litigation and enforcement work related to intimate image publication.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. Social media platforms and similar websites would be required to remove such content within 48 hours after receiving a complaint from the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

bill.title: Dolores River National Conservation Area and Special Management Area Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 480.

industries.rationale: The bill addresses livestock use within the conservation areas, which affects ranching operations on federal grazing allotments.
The conservation and special management area designations would likely restrict or prohibit new mining claims and mineral extraction on the designated federal lands.
Conservation area designations typically restrict or prohibit new energy development, potentially affecting oil and gas leasing rights on the affected federal lands.
The bill's focus on protecting recreational and scenic values may affect tourism and outdoor recreation businesses operating in or near the designated areas.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create two protected areas along the Dolores River in Colorado: a 52,872-acre National Conservation Area on Bureau of Land Management land and a 15,452-acre Special Management Area in the San Juan National Forest. The bill requires management plans for both areas, preserves tribal access for traditional uses, prohibits road construction and motorized vehicles in the Ponderosa Gorge portion, and bars commercial timber harvesting there. It also establishes an advisory council and removes certain river segments from consideration for Wild and Scenic River designation.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who drives. People who live near or work on federal land.

bill.latestActionText: Held at the desk.

Federal promotion of domestic and international tourism to music and sports attractions would directly increase demand for hotels, travel services, and related hospitality businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the National Travel and Tourism Office within the Department of Commerce to actively promote tourism to music festivals, concert venues, and other music-related sites in the United States, targeting both domestic and international travelers. It also expands the office's existing sports-promotion duties to include international tourism for sports events. The office must report its activities and results to Congress within one year and every two years thereafter.

bill.title: Small County PILT Parity Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 474.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects federal payments to county and local governments that host tax-exempt federal lands.
Counties with significant federal land often host mining operations on those lands, and changes to local revenue formulas may indirectly affect permitting and local fiscal capacity.
Federal lands in small counties frequently include oil, gas, or coal extraction sites, and local revenue changes may affect the fiscal environment for these operations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would modify federal payments to local governments that contain tax-exempt federal land. Specifically, it appears to adjust the Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) formula for small counties, which compensates localities for property-tax revenue they cannot collect on federally owned land. Without access to the bill text, the precise nature of the change to the formula or eligibility criteria cannot be described.
